name: Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds)
builder: Sawai Pratap Singh; architect Lal Chand Ustad
overview:
Hawa Mahal, the Palace of Winds, is the iconic pink sandstone facade that stands on a busy street in the old city of Jaipur, Rajasthan. It was built in 1799 by Maharaja Sawai Pratap Singh, and is credited to the architect Lal Chand Ustad. The building was designed as an extension of the City Palace, so that the women of the royal household could watch street festivals and processions without being seen, following the custom of purdah.

The beauty of the Hawa Mahal lies in its honeycomb-like front. Five storeys high, it is covered with 953 small windows called jharokhas, each with delicate lattice work and tiny balconies. The pink and red sandstone, finished with white lime detailing, glows warmly in the early sun. The structure is sometimes said to resemble the crown of Krishna, and the repeating pattern of windows gives it a rhythm and lightness unusual for a building of such height.

Architecturally, it combines Rajput and Mughal elements, with domed canopies, curved cornices and fine carving. The building is surprisingly shallow, little more than a screen with narrow rooms and ramps behind it. The many small openings and courtyards help air flow through the structure, which kept the rooms cool in the Rajasthani summer, and gave the palace its name.

Jaipur itself was founded in 1727 by Sawai Jai Singh II as one of India's first planned cities, and the old city was later painted pink, a colour traditionally associated with hospitality, for a royal visit in the 1870s. Hawa Mahal is part of the walled city of Jaipur, which was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2019.

Hawa Mahal is best photographed from across the street, where cafes offer views, especially in the morning light. The entrance is from the rear, and inside there is a small museum and rooftop views. Nearby are the City Palace, Jantar Mantar and the bazaars of Johari Bazaar and Tripolia. Check opening times and ticket rules with official sources.
